newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P says affirms Boral's ratings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P says affirms Boral's ratings.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday that it had affirmed the "A" long-term credit rating and "A-1" commercial paper ratings of Australian industrial group Boral Ltd and its guaranteed U.S. subsidiary.
The ratings outlook remained negative, S&P said.

The affirmation followed an announcement by Boral that it was planning to float its gas distribution network, raising more than A$850 million. Boral would hold a 19.9 percent interest in the new company, to be called Envestra Ltd.

S&P said it regarded the float as strategically neutral, given the relatively small size of the division's revenues and profit contributions to Boral's revenue base, and a favourable operational and management relationship with Envestra.
"These benefits are offset by the divestment of a low-risk business that generates relatively stable operating cash flows," S&P said.
Boral said funds raised from the sale would initially be used to retire debt but could also be used to fund purchases.
Boral also said the transaction would be earnings positive from the outset.

"Boral's negative outlook reflects the absence of a foreseeably material recovery in the domestic building markets and uncertainty concerning the quality and stability of earnings that will be generated from sale proceeds, notwithstanding the temporary benefit the transaction will provide to the company's balance sheet," S&P said.
